\chapter{How It Felt, What I Hope}
\label{ch:ar-how-it-felt-what-i-hope}
\hlchaptermodality{289}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say how an experience felt and what I hope, dream or want to become.}

Complete AR-R289-feelings-and-hopes: how an experience felt, with kuntu and -an, and what you hope for, with atamannā an.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{كنت} \ar{سعيدا} (kuntu saʿīdan)}{كنت سعيدا (kuntu saʿīdan)}]{\ar{كنت} \ar{سعيدا} (kuntu saʿīdan) — I was happy}

\label{lesson:AR-C289-kuntu-saidan}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}I missed the train\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}who is in charge here?\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{Fātanī al-qiṭār}, \emph{man al-masʾūl hunā?})

A story of a trip is not finished until you say how it felt.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: kāna and the -an}]
Today needs no verb: \emph{anā saʿīd}, I'm happy. In the past \emph{kāna} comes in, and the word that describes takes \emph{-an}, the accusative:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ar{كنت} \ar{سعيدا}.} — \emph{kuntu saʿīdan} — I was happy.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ar{كانت} \ar{حزينة}.} — \emph{kānat ḥazīna} — She was sad.
\end{quote}

On most words the \emph{-an} is written with a final \textbf{\ar{ا}}: \textbf{\ar{سعيدا}}, \textbf{\ar{متعبا}}, \textbf{\ar{غاضبا}}. On a word ending in \textbf{\ar{ة}} it is not written, and at the end of a sentence it is not said: \emph{kānat ḥazīna}. You met it already in \emph{kuntu mutʿaban} and \emph{kāna aṭ-ṭaqs jamīlan}.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: I felt}]
To name the feeling as a noun, say \emph{shaʿartu bi-}, \textquotedblleft{}I felt\textquotedblright{}, with the feeling after \emph{bi-}:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ar{شعرت} \ar{بالخوف} \ar{عندما} \ar{طارت} \ar{الطائرة}.} — \emph{shaʿartu bi-l-khawf ʿindamā ṭārat aṭ-ṭāʾira} — I felt afraid when the plane took off.
\end{quote}

Word for word, \textquotedblleft{}I felt fear\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Aḥsastu bi-}, from \emph{aḥassa}, to feel, says the same: \emph{aḥsastu bi-l-khawf}.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I'm happy\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}I was happy\textquotedblright{} — \emph{anā saʿīd}, \emph{kuntu saʿīdan}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}She was sad\textquotedblright{} — \emph{kānat ḥazīna}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}We were tired\textquotedblright{} — \emph{kunnā mutʿabīn}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I felt afraid when the plane took off\textquotedblright{} — \emph{shaʿartu bi-l-khawf ʿindamā ṭārat aṭ-ṭāʾira}
  \item a feeling and what came of it — \emph{kuntu ghāḍiban, fa-kharajtu}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}I was happy\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Kuntu saʿīdan}}, with \emph{-an}.) Why the \emph{-an}? (\textbf{Kāna gives it to the word that describes.}) \textquotedblleft{}I felt afraid\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Shaʿartu bi-l-khawf.}})
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تجربة} (tajriba)}{تجربة (tajriba)}]{\ar{تجربة} (tajriba) — an experience}

\label{lesson:AR-C289-tajriba}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}I was happy\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}I felt afraid\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{Kuntu saʿīdan}, \emph{shaʿartu bi-l-khawf}.)

You have a verb for trying on a coat, \emph{jarraba}. Its noun covers much more than coats.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تجربة}}
\textbf{\ar{تجربة}} — \emph{tajriba} — \textquotedblleft{}an experience\textquotedblright{}; also \textquotedblleft{}a try, an experiment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ar{كانت} \ar{الرحلة} \ar{تجربة} \ar{جديدة}.} — \emph{kānat ar-riḥla tajribatan jadīda} — The trip was a new experience.
\end{quote}

It is \emph{kāna}'s \emph{-an} again: \emph{tajribatan}, though the \textbf{\ar{ة}} hides it on the page. \emph{Tajriba mumtiʿa} is an enjoyable experience; \emph{tajriba mumilla}, a boring one.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تجربة}} (\emph{tajriba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-r-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to try, to test\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives \emph{jarraba} as making trial of a thing, time after time, and \emph{tajriba} as its noun: a trial. An experience, in Arabic, is something you have tried.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{tajriba}, then \emph{jarraba}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}The trip was a new experience\textquotedblright{} — \emph{kānat ar-riḥla tajribatan jadīda}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}an enjoyable experience\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}a boring one\textquotedblright{} — \emph{tajriba mumtiʿa}, \emph{tajriba mumilla}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}In my opinion it was a good experience\textquotedblright{} — \emph{fī raʾyī kānat tajribatan jayyida}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تجربة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An experience; a try\textquotedblright{}.) Which verb shares its root? (\emph{\textbf{Jarraba}}, to try.) \textquotedblleft{}A new experience\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Tajriba jadīda.}})
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أتمنى} \ar{أن} (atamannā an)}{أتمنى أن (atamannā an)}]{\ar{أتمنى} \ar{أن} (atamannā an) — I hope to}

\label{lesson:AR-C289-atamanna-an}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}the trip was a new experience\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{Kānat ar-riḥla tajribatan jadīda}.) Then \textquotedblleft{}I felt afraid\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{Shaʿartu bi-l-khawf}.)

That was the past. Now turn ahead: what you hope for, what you dream of, what you want to become.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: atamannā an, aḥlumu bi-}]
\emph{Tamannā}, to wish, from chapter one hundred and fourteen, has the present \emph{atamannā}, I hope, I wish. \emph{An} and the subjunctive follow it, as after \emph{urīdu}:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ar{أتمنى} \ar{أن} \ar{أجد} \ar{وظيفة} \ar{جديدة}.} — \emph{atamannā an ajida waẓīfa jadīda} — I hope to find a new job.
\end{quote}

\emph{Ajida} is the subjunctive of \emph{ajidu}, I find, from \emph{wajada}; the \emph{w} has dropped again.

For a dream, use the verb of \emph{ḥulm}: \emph{aḥlumu bi-}, I dream of, with a noun after \emph{bi-}: \emph{aḥlumu bi-riḥla ṭawīla}, I dream of a long journey.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: what you want to become}]
\emph{Aṣbaḥa}, to become, behaves like \emph{kāna}: what it becomes takes \emph{-an}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ar{أريد} \ar{أن} \ar{أصبح} \ar{مهندسا}.} — \emph{urīdu an uṣbiḥa muhandisan} — I want to become an engineer.
\end{quote}

\emph{Uṣbiḥa} is its subjunctive, after \emph{an}. In the past: \emph{aṣbaḥtu muhandisan}, I became an engineer.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I hope to find a new job\textquotedblright{} — \emph{atamannā an ajida waẓīfa jadīda}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I dream of a long journey\textquotedblright{} — \emph{aḥlumu bi-riḥla ṭawīla}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I want to become an engineer\textquotedblright{} — \emph{urīdu an uṣbiḥa muhandisan}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}She wants to become a doctor\textquotedblright{} — \emph{turīdu an tuṣbiḥa ṭabība}
  \item your own: \emph{atamannā an} and one thing, then \emph{urīdu an uṣbiḥa} and one job
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}I hope to\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Atamannā an.}}) \textquotedblleft{}I dream of\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Aḥlumu bi-.}}) \textquotedblleft{}To become\textquotedblright{}, after \emph{an}? (\emph{\textbf{Uṣbiḥa.}}) What does \emph{aṣbaḥa} give the word after it? (\textbf{The \emph{-an}}, as \emph{kāna} does.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(review)]{Review — how it felt, and what comes next}

\label{lesson:AR-R289-feelings-and-hopes}



\begin{quote}
Buy a return ticket and ask the price. (\emph{Tadhkirat dhahāb wa-iyāb, min faḍlik. Bi-kam at-tadhkira?}) Then report a problem and ask for the person in charge. (\emph{Fātanī al-qiṭār. Urīdu an atakallama maʿa al-masʾūl}.)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Three lessons, and an experience can be told from both ends. Looking back: \emph{kuntu saʿīdan}, \emph{kānat ḥazīna}, \emph{shaʿartu bi-l-khawf}, \emph{kānat tajribatan jadīda}. Looking ahead: \emph{atamannā an}, \emph{aḥlumu bi-}, \emph{urīdu an uṣbiḥa}.

Both ends in one breath:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ar{كانت} \ar{تجربة} \ar{صعبة،} \ar{لكنني} \ar{أتمنى} \ar{أن} \ar{أسافر} \ar{مرة} \ar{أخرى}.} — \emph{kānat tajribatan ṣaʿba, lākinnanī atamannā an usāfira marratan ukhrā} — It was a hard experience, but I hope to travel again.
\end{quote}
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}We were happy\textquotedblright{} — \emph{kunnā saʿīdīn}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}He wants to become an actor\textquotedblright{} — \emph{yurīdu an yuṣbiḥa mumaththilan}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}The barber was angry\textquotedblright{} — \emph{kāna al-ḥallāq ghāḍiban}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I told my grandmother how the trip was\textquotedblright{} — \emph{ḥakaytu li-jaddatī kayfa kānat ar-riḥla}
  \item how your last trip felt, and one thing you hope for next time
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}I was tired\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Kuntu mutʿaban.}}) \textquotedblleft{}I felt afraid\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Shaʿartu bi-l-khawf.}}) \textquotedblleft{}I hope to travel\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Atamannā an usāfira.}}) \textquotedblleft{}An experience\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{Tajriba.}})
\end{tcolorbox}
